source_text: Quod quoniam nec ratio sustinet ulla, nec pietas; aut doce, vel posse esse, vel iustum esse, imputari cuiquam naturale peccatum; aut a Scripturarum sanctarum contaminatione discedito, quarum sententiis sanciri aestimas quod iniquum cogeris confiteri.
pass_a_gloss: Which since neither any reason sustains, nor piety; either teach that a natural sin is able to be, or that it is just, to be imputed to anyone; or depart from contamination of the Holy Scriptures, by whose sentences you estimate that to be sanctioned which you are compelled to confess unjust.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Since neither any sound reasoning nor piety permits that, either show that imputing a sin inherent in nature to someone is possible, or that it is just, or cease contaminating the Holy Scriptures. You suppose their statements authorize what you are compelled to admit is unjust.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
